articles.title: Europe Looks Beyond America's Nuclear Shield As Macron Offers 10 Countries An Alternative | Report
articles.description: Ten European countries are reportedly discussing a French-led nuclear deterrence initiative as questions grow over whether Europe can continue relying almost entirely on America’s nuclear umbrella. At the centre of the proposal is France’s concept of “forward deterrence,” which could eventually involve French nuclear-capable Rafale fighters operating farther across Europe. Britain, Germany, Poland, Greece and Nordic countries are among those reportedly involved in discussions. France maintains an independent nuclear arsenal, publicly estimated at roughly 290 warheads, giving Emmanuel Macron something most European governments do not possess: a deterrent that does not ultimately depend on a US president authorising nuclear escalation. But control would remain firmly in Paris. Participating countries could potentially host or support the posture, while the French president would retain the final decision over nuclear use. For Washington, the political implication is significant: European interest in a French alternative reflects growing debate over whether America’s security guarantee alone remains sufficient.

articles.title: ITBP’s New Strategy: Drones, Shaurya Commandos & Bunkers to Counter China’s LAC Challenge
articles.description: Drones above the mountains, specialised commandos on the ground and underground shelters along the frontier. The Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) is upgrading its preparations along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) with China. In this Defence HQ explainer, we examine the force’s expanding drone capabilities, the role of its Shaurya commando platoons and plans to develop underground shelters at forward posts.ITBP Director General Shatrujeet Singh Kapoor has outlined a ₹400-crore allocation, with 70% earmarked for strengthening drone warfare capabilities. Separately, the Home Ministry has given in-principle approval to a ₹4,000-crore modernisation scheme that includes a proposed ₹1,000 crore for drone and anti-drone systems. The force is also raising Shaurya commando platoons, training personnel for high-altitude contingencies and developing better-protected infrastructure for troops deployed in extreme Himalayan conditions. articles.title: Kharge’s ‘Modi Ka Baap’ Remark Sparks Nationwide BJP Protests | Congress Faces Backlash | News18
articles.description: A fresh political confrontation has erupted between the BJP and Congress after Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge’s remark about Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s late father at an event in Patna triggered nationwide protests on October 26. The controversy began on October 25 during a programme marking the birth anniversary of Bihar’s first chief minister, Shri Krishna Singh. While speaking about alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, Kharge was interrupted by an audience member. His response — “Modi ka baap bhi jayega” — drew sharp criticism from BJP leaders, who accused him of crossing the limits of political decorum. The BJP organised demonstrations in several cities, including Delhi, Patna, Bengaluru, Lucknow and Jammu, demanding an apology from Kharge and Congress leader Rahul Gandhi. Protests included marches, slogans and effigy or poster burnings.
